Where it began

Moeen Ali was born on 18 June 1987 in Sparkhill, Birmingham. Cricket ran in the family: his first cousin Kabir Ali grew up on the same street, and his brothers Kadeer and Omar played too.

Warwickshire signed him at 15, and he went on to captain England at the 2006 Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka. First-team chances were scarce, so in the autumn of 2006 he moved to Worcestershire. He made 250 there against Glamorgan, his highest first-class score, and in 2013 he piled up 1,375 runs, more than anyone else in the first-class game that summer, and was named the PCA player of the year.

The player

He made his England debut in 2014 and hit his first Test hundred in only his second match, against Sri Lanka. He played 68 Tests between 2014 and 2023, making 3,094 runs at 28.13 with five hundreds and a best of 155 not out. With his off-spin he took 204 wickets at 37.31, including five five-wicket hauls and one ten-wicket match, with a best of 6 for 53.

The summer of 2017 was his finest. Against South Africa he took ten wickets in the first Test, then in the third, at The Oval, wrapped up victory with a hat-trick, which no England spinner had managed since 1938–39 and nobody at all had done in a Test at that ground. He retired from Tests in 2021, came back for the 2023 Ashes, and took his 200th wicket there, Steve Smith, before leaving Tests for good. In white-ball cricket he helped England win the 2019 World Cup and the 2022 T20 World Cup, and he captained them in T20 internationals.

What made him special

He could score fast when it suited: one ODI hundred against the West Indies took him just 53 balls. England moved him up and down the order, even asking him to open, and he went wherever he was sent. He kept adding to his bowling too, trying the doosra at the urging of Saeed Ajmal.

If he had a nemesis, it was an Australian off-spinner. On the 2017–18 Ashes tour Nathan Lyon got him seven times in nine innings, which suggests the two of them knew each other's games rather well.

Away from the middle

He was named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year, was made an OBE in 2022 for services to cricket, and Coventry University gave him an honorary doctorate in 2024. He has also been an ambassador for StreetChance, which offers free cricket coaching in deprived areas. His autobiography, Moeen, came out in 2018, and he is a lifelong Liverpool supporter.

He won the IPL twice with Chennai Super Kings, in 2021 and 2023, captained Worcestershire Rapids to their first T20 Blast title in 2018 and led Birmingham Phoenix in The Hundred.

And finally

In a Test at Chittagong on England's 2016–17 tour of Bangladesh he was given out three times in the same innings, all off Shakib Al Hasan, and reviewed every one of them successfully. No batsman had ever won three reviews in a row in one innings before. Few have had a busier session of being out without actually going anywhere.
